sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter (Zet) /tsɛt/ makes the sound /ts/ in the word (Zug) /tsuːk/, which means train. It has two sounds in German, but one sound is far more common. In borrowed words it sounds different. Listen carefully to how native speakers pronounce it in everyday speech.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: To make the sound /ts/, press your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Stop the breath, then release it into a sharp hiss. Do not use your voice. For the sound /z/, bring your teeth close together and blow air gently. Keep your vocal cords buzzing. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration on that second sound.

sections.title: Where each sound appears
paragraphs: In almost all German words, the letter sounds like /ts/. You hear this in the word (Zimmer) /ˈtsɪmɐ/. In recent loanwords borrowed from English, it keeps the original English sound /z/. You can hear this second pronunciation in the word (Zoom) /zuːm/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not pronounce this letter like the English letter z in zoo when reading German words. That soft buzzing sound is wrong for regular German vocabulary. Start with a firm t sound and slide instantly into an s sound. Think of the ending of the English word cats. Make the burst crisp and sudden.
